1. The completed restricted sampler

Here is the precise new positive result.

Expand each local Hamiltonian term into at most $4^k$ Pauli terms, and put

$$d_{\mathrm P}=4^k d.$$

Each resulting coefficient has magnitude at most $J$. In each schedule segment, color the term-conflict graph with at most

$$c=kd_{\mathrm P}$$

colors, padding segments to the same declared number of colors.

Choose fixed connected lattice balls containing the terms assigned to each anchor. Let $s$ bound their size, $h$ their cover multiplicity, and $\ell_0\ge1$ their diameter. These constants are computable from the fixed locality class.

A conservative sufficient time condition is

$$\boxed{\quad
JT\le \frac{1}{24shd_{\mathrm P}c}.
\quad} \tag{1}$$

Theorem. Under (1), the native unital process

$$\mathcal L_t=-i[H(t),\cdot]+\gamma\sum_i(E_i-\mathrm{Id})$$

admits an unconditional TV-$\epsilon$ sampler for the entire supplied one-site POVM output law, with worst-case bit work

$$\boxed{\quad
\operatorname{poly}_{a,k,d}
\!\left(n,B,1+g^{-1},\epsilon^{-1}\right).
\quad} \tag{2}$$

It covers every supplied rational product preparation and every rational piecewise Hamiltonian schedule satisfying the declared bounds. The schedule, output lists, arithmetic, truncations and random bits are included.

This is a proved and costed mathematical algorithm using the accepted finite-bit MPS primitive. I have not executed new general sampler software.

Why this is a generative result

The construction produces one complete correlated output record. Its local conditional distributions come from explicitly constructed positive rational MPS states. It does not request a conditional-probability oracle, and its error analysis does not divide by the probability of a rare observed record.

The useful change of method is to update a classical output record gate by gate, while controlling the error averaged over the records that actually occur. The gate-by-gate framework and averaged postmeasurement-impurity machinery are credited to Bene Watts, Gosset, Liu and Soleimanifar. Their theorem does not itself supply the physical-time bound or the finite-bit native construction below. arxiv.org [https://arxiv.org/html/2407.21203v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

3. Constructing and sampling the local joint laws

Let $P_j$ be the output distribution of the $j$-th pure circuit prefix. Suppose the next unitary gate acts on $A$. Then

$$(P_{j-1})_{A^c}=(P_j)_{A^c}.$$

An exact classical update would retain the outside record and redraw $A$ from $P_j(A\mid A^c)$.

The algorithm instead uses a shield $B$ of radius

$$R=O_{a,k,d}\!\left(\log\frac{M}{\epsilon}\right),$$

where $M$ is the paid number of gate and coin locations. Equation (6) makes the error of discarding the more distant record $O(\epsilon/M)$.

The remaining joint law on $AB$ is constructed as follows.

- 
Add another spatial buffer. Restrict the fixed unitary history to a larger patch $W$. Time-dependent locality gives a reduced-$AB$ trace-error bound. Choose the buffer from that explicit bound so its contribution is $O(\epsilon/M)$. This use of locality controls a finite marginal; it does not assert a global sampling theorem from locality alone. arxiv.org [https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.4210v2?utm_source=chatgpt.com]


- 
Compile a positive rational MPS on $W$. The patch has

$$|W|=O_{a,k,d}\!\left(\log^2\frac{M}{\epsilon}\right).$$

In a row ordering, its integrated crossing strength is

$$\Chi=O_{a,k,d}(JT\,R).$$

The accepted pure-history cut-parameter compiler therefore costs a polynomial times $e^{O(\Chi)}$. Since $JT$ is bounded and $R$ is logarithmic, this cost is polynomial.


- 
Compute the conditional from that positive law. Let $Q_{AB}$ be the measured joint law of the rational MPS. Contract its transfer matrices with the observed $B$ effects and each possible output on the constant-size gate support $A$. These are paid rational contractions.


The crucial error conversion is

$$\boxed{
\sum_b P_B(b)\,
\operatorname{TV}\!\left(P(A\mid b),Q(A\mid b)\right)
\le 2\,\operatorname{TV}(P_{AB},Q_{AB}).
}
\tag{7}$$

It remains valid when $Q_B(b)=0$, provided an arbitrary conditional is assigned there.

To prove it, replace the $B$ marginal of $Q$ by $P_B$, retaining its conditionals. This replacement costs exactly $\operatorname{TV}(P_B,Q_B)$, which is at most the joint TV distance. A triangle inequality proves (7).

Thus the patch reader needs absolute joint accuracy, even though the eventual update is conditional. It never needs to approximate a tiny physical prefix probability relatively.

1. Replica cancellation and amplification

The cancellation is valid.

For a connected component $X$, every doubled local generator supported in $X$ commutes with the swap of the two $X$ registers. Its connected kernel $K_X$ therefore does also. The initial product replica vector is invariant under every such swap.

After applying the same rank-one measurement bra to both copies of $B$, a swap on $X\subseteq A\cup B$ becomes a swap on $A\cap X$. For a retained disjoint component family, the components intersecting $A$, together with uncovered sites of $A$, partition $A$. The resulting vector is invariant under their product, namely $\mathrm{Swap}_A$. This proves its annihilation by $P_A^-$.

$$-i(H_\alpha\otimes I+I\otimes H_\alpha)$$

has projective-norm operator bound $2\|H_\alpha\|$ even with arbitrary untouched spatial registers. Products of words consequently have the required product bounds. The restricted exterior is $U_{\rm restricted}\otimes U_{\rm restricted}$, with norm one. No unamplified-to-amplified norm equivalence is being assumed.

I also checked the rank-one measurement map. Its projective-to-$\ell^1$-Hilbert contraction follows directly from completeness and Cauchy–Schwarz. Partial swap is used only as a Hilbert-norm contraction, so no problematic projective-norm bound for partial swap is required.
